Reference / archive/zip

archive/zip#

ZIP archives (#185): ZipArchive reads one from bytes, ZipWriting writes one to a Writing; members are stored or deflated, and ZIP64 is read and written.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

for ZipArchive(bytes).entries() -> entry {
    entry.name();
    await entry.bytes(limit: 10485760);
}

let zip = ZipWriting(destination: output);
zip.add(name: "a.txt", bytes: data);
zip.close(); // the central directory goes out here

Description#

ZIP archives (#185): ZipArchive reads one from bytes, ZipWriting writes one to a Writing; members are stored or deflated, and ZIP64 is read and written.

Reading trusts nothing in the archive:

  • every name goes through ArchivePath, so an absolute name, "..", a backslash or a drive prefix is UnsafeArchivePath, and a name given twice is DuplicateArchivePath;
  • ArchiveLimits bound the entries, their declared sizes and the names: 65 536 entries, 1 GiB a member, 4 GiB in all and names of 4 096 characters, unless given;
  • members may not overlap one another or the central directory;
  • bytes(limit) never makes more than the declared size or the limit and checks the CRC-32, so a member that expands beyond what it declares is InvalidZip instead of a bomb;
  • encrypted members, multi-disk archives and methods other than stored and deflated are UnsupportedZip.

A ZIP method name, not a wire identifier or a promise of an installed codec. Reading and writing support stored and deflated; the other names are writing choices for which no codec is installed.

object ZipCompression#

object ZipCompression

Immutable choice of ZIP method and effective compression level. Construction validates local invariants; observations have no I/O or provider discovery. Defaults are stored=0, deflated=6, bzip2=9, lzma=0, zstandard=3. Explicit levels: deflated 0..9, bzip2 1..9, zstandard -131072..22 inclusive. Zstandard 0 resolves to 3. DEFLATE 0 remains a distinct real level. Stored/LZMA reject every explicit level, even 0; their observed zero means no configurable ZIP level, not an LZMA preset. InvalidArgument is immediate. The fixed Zstandard range does not depend on an installed host version. No clamping, implicit method, ambient defaults, resources or compression.

let stored = ZipCompression(ZipMethod.stored);
let chosen = ZipCompression(ZipMethod.deflated, 9);
chosen.method(); // ZipMethod.deflated
chosen.level();  // 9; this value itself does not compress anything

object ZipArchiveEntry#

object ZipArchiveEntry

One member's explicit ZIP writing request: an archive value paired with a validated compression choice. Both coordinates are retained unchanged. Binding and observing them never calls entry methods, visits payload, reads metadata, compresses bytes or owns/closes a resource. No format capability is implied: a writer must check entry kind, metadata and codec support before output.

The wrapper is not itself an ArchiveEntry. Unwrap deliberately to use ordinary archive visitors or writers. A second compression choice creates a separate request for the same immutable entry; neither request changes the other.

let request = ZipArchiveEntry(file, ZipCompression(ZipMethod.stored));
request.entry().accept(visitor); // only this explicit call visits file

object ZipWriting#

object ZipWriting does Closing

A ZIP archive written member by member to a Writing; close() writes the central directory. A member is deflated when that makes it smaller, and stored otherwise; a name ending in "/" is a directory with no bytes. Names go through ArchivePath; one given twice is DuplicateArchivePath. Times are 1980-01-01 00:00, so the same members make the same archive.
